**Paid Sick Leave – California & New York**

---

### 1.  Why a single policy can satisfy both states

| Issue | California (HWHA) | New York (PSLL) |
|-------|-------------------|-----------------|
| **Accrual rate** | 1 hr for every 30 hrs worked | Same – 1 hr per 30 hrs |
| **Maximum accrual** | Employers may cap at **48 hrs** (or 6 days) | Same – max **48 hrs** per year |
| **Eligibility** | Must have completed **90 days** of service | Same – 90‑day waiting period |
| **Use‑within‑year requirement** | None; employees can use leave at any time after accruing | Employees must be able to use all accrued sick leave within the calendar year it is earned (unless they carry over up to 40 hrs) |
| **Carryover** | Unlimited unless capped by employer | Up to **40 hrs** (or 24 hrs if the employer has a policy that limits carry‑over) |
| **Family‑member definition** | Spouse, domestic partner, child, parent, sibling, grandparent, grandchild, in‑laws, and any person who is a dependent under the employee’s care | Same set of relatives; “family member” includes anyone who is a family member of the employee |
| **Preventive care** | Covered (e.g., routine check‑ups) | Covered |

Because both states allow a maximum accrual of 48 hrs and require a 90‑day waiting period, a single policy that:

* accrues at 1 hr per 30 hrs worked,
* caps accrual at **48 hrs** per calendar year,
* allows use after the 90‑day mark,
* permits carryover up to **40 hrs** (NY requirement) – which is fully permissible under CA law,

will satisfy each state’s statutory minimums and maximum limits. The policy does **not** give employees more leave than either state requires, because it never exceeds the 48‑hr cap that both laws allow.

---

### 2.  Draft Policy

> **Title:** Paid Sick Leave (PSL)  
> **Effective Date:** [Insert date]  
> **Locations Covered:** All California and New York offices  

#### 2.1 Purpose
To provide employees with paid sick leave in compliance with the Healthy Workplaces, Healthy Families Act of 2014 (California) and the New York State Paid Sick Leave Law.

#### 2.2 Eligibility
* Full‑time employees who have completed **90 consecutive days** of employment are eligible.
* Part‑time employees accrue proportionally based on hours worked.

#### 2.3 Accrual & Maximum
| Item | Detail |
|------|--------|
| **Accrual Rate** | Employees earn **1 hr** of paid sick leave for every **30 hrs** worked. |
| **Cap** | Accrual stops once an employee reaches **48 hrs** in a calendar year. |
| **Start of Accrual** | Accrual begins on the employee’s 91st day of service. |
| **Monthly Calculation** | At month‑end, hours worked ÷ 30 = hrs accrued (rounded to nearest quarter hour). |

#### 2.4 Use of Sick Leave
Employees may use accrued sick leave for:

1. **Illness or injury** of the employee.
2. **Medical/dental appointments** for the employee.
3. **Illness, injury, or medical condition** of a family member (see § 2.6).
4. **Medical/dental appointments** for a family member.
5. **Preventive health care services** for the employee or a family member.

*Employees must notify their manager as soon as possible and at least **one hour** before scheduled work unless an emergency prevents advance notice.*

#### 2.5 Family Member Definition
For this policy, “family member” includes:

- Spouse or domestic partner
- Child (biological, adopted, step)
- Parent (biological, adoptive, step)
- Sibling (full, half, step)
- Grandparent, grandchild
- In‑laws
- Any person who is a dependent under the employee’s care

#### 2.6 Carryover & Use‑Within‑Year
* **Carryover** – Unused sick leave may be carried over to the next calendar year up to **40 hrs**. Any unused hours beyond 40 are forfeited at year‑end.
* **Use‑within‑year** – Employees must be able to use all accrued sick leave within the calendar year it is earned (NY requirement). The carryover limit satisfies this provision.

#### 2.7 Separate Paid Time Off
The company also offers **10 days (80 hrs)** of paid time off for vacation, personal reasons, or other non‑sick purposes. PTO and PSL are separate; employees may use either as needed but cannot combine them to exceed statutory limits.

#### 2.8 Recordkeeping & Balance Tracking
* Employees will view their accrued and used sick leave balances in the HR portal.
* Managers must approve requests and record usage in the system.

#### 2.9 Compliance & Enforcement
This policy complies with California’s HWHA and New York’s PSLL. The company will not reduce an employee’s accrued PSL below statutory minimums or cap accrual at less than 48 hrs per year.

#### 2.10 Amendments
The company reserves the right to amend this policy as required by law or business needs, with prior notice to employees.

#### 2.11 Contact Information
For questions about paid sick leave, contact HR:
* Email: **hr@somedomain.com**
* Phone: **(555) 123‑4567**

---

### 3.  Summary of Key Differences

| Feature | California | New York |
|---------|------------|----------|
| **Carryover** | Unlimited unless capped by employer | Up to 40 hrs (or 24 hrs if policy limits carryover) |
| **Use‑within‑year** | No requirement | Must use all accrued within the year it is earned |
| **Accrual cap** | 48 hrs | 48 hrs |
| **Waiting period** | 90 days | 90 days |

By adopting the above policy, the company meets both states’ statutory minimums and maximum limits while keeping a single, clear set of rules for all employees.
